name: Common Cystic Lymphatic Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Cystic Lymphatic Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of soft, compressible, and transilluminant cystic masses typically located in the cervicofacial region
Ultrasound and MRI showing multiloculated cystic lesions with thin septations without solid components
Biopsy demonstrating dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells without atypia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus confirmatory imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not always required if clinical and imaging findings are conclusive.

searchTerms: cyst with multiple compartments on scan

common.symptomName: Localized pain or discomfort due to mass effect
searchTerms: discomfort due to mass pressing on tissues

common.symptomName: Recurrent infections or cellulitis over the lesion
Difficulty swallowing or breathing if lesion compresses airway
searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to airway compression
airway or swallowing problems from mass

occasional.symptomName: Hemorrhage within cyst causing sudden enlargement
searchTerms: bleeding inside cyst causing sudden growth
cyst enlarges quickly due to hemorrhage
sudden cyst swelling from internal bleeding
nerve pain or weakness from compression
neurological symptoms due to mass effect

occasional.symptomName: Lymphorrhea or leakage of lymphatic fluid

searchTerms: fluid buildup in limb from lymph blockage

laboratory: Normal blood counts unless secondary infection present
Lymphatic fluid analysis showing proteinaceous fluid with lymphocytes
imaging: Ultrasound: multiloculated cystic masses with thin septations
MRI: well-defined cystic lesions with fluid signal intensity, no solid enhancement
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology: dilated lymphatic channels lined by flat endothelial cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of blood flow on Doppler ultrasound
Rapid postnatal growth followed by involution
Red or purple discoloration of skin
Typically located along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid
No multiloculated cystic appearance on imaging

redFlags: Signs of infection such as fever and erythema
Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular Anomalies Classification: Recommendations From the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
